properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 15 at 4:42PM MDT until September 15 at 6:45PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
At 442 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
moderate rain over the western portion of the Frijoles Burn Scar as
well as areas west of the burn scar to including Cundiyo. Between
0.50 and 0.75 inches of rain have fallen over the western portions of
the burn scar, with up to 1.5 inches along Highway 503 southwest of
Cundiyo. Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.50 inches are possible
in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will impact the Rio Frijoles,
Rio Medio and Chimayo Creek as well as Camino del Canon, County Road
127 and Camino del Molino. The debris flow can consist of rock, mud,
vegetation and other loose materials. Flooding will also impact
Cundiyo and Highway 503.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Frijoles Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Frijoles Burn Scar.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Chimayo, Cundiyo, Rio Chiquito, Nambe Pueblo, Nambe Lake and
Cordova.
properties.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks, streams and ditches in
the Frijoles Burn Scar. Severe debris flows can also be anticipated
across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away in places. If
you encounter flood waters, climb to safety.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 15 at 6:20PM CDT until September 15 at 6:30PM CDT by NWS Kansas City/Pleasant Hill MO
properties.description:
At 619 PM CDT, a severe thunderstorm was located near Union Star, or
12 miles west of Maysville, moving east at 25 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and nickel size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

Locations impacted include...
Union Star, Clarksdale, Cosby, and Helena.
properties.instruction:
For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 15 at 2:42PM MDT until September 15 at 5:45PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
FFWGJT

The National Weather Service in Grand Junction has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Eastern San Miguel County in southwestern Colorado...

* Until 545 PM MDT.

* At 242 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Sawpit, Fall Creek and Placerville.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Fall Creek, Deep Creek, Big Bear Creek, Muddy Creek, Saltado Creek,
South Fork San Miguel River, Dolores River, Specie Creek, San
Miguel River, Leopard Creek and Alder Creek.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Highway 145 is prone to rockslides and mudslides in heavy rain. Stay
alert for rocks and debris on roads, and avoid driving on flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 15 at 6:18PM CDT until September 15 at 6:30PM CDT by NWS Lincoln IL
properties.description:
At 618 PM CDT, a severe thunderstorm was located near Carlock, or 10
miles southeast of Eureka, moving northeast at 25 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and half dollar size hail.

SOURCE...Emergency management.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage to
roofs, siding, and trees.

This severe thunderstorm will remain over mainly rural areas of
southeastern Woodford and northwestern McLean Counties.

This includes the following highways...
Interstate 39 between mile markers 3 and 12.
Interstate 74 between mile markers 113 and 125.
properties.instruction:
For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

Continuous cloud to ground lightning is occurring with this storm.
Move indoors immediately. Lightning is one of nature's leading
killers. Remember, if you can hear thunder, you are close enough to
be struck by lightning.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 15 at 5:05PM MDT until September 15 at 7:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
At 505 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated light to moderate rain
continues across the warned area. Between 1.25 and 1.75 inches of
rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.25 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to
begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Southern McKinley County.

Flash flooding can be expected along Highway 36, Knife Hill Canyon
Road and Indian Reservation Road 9. Elevated water flows are also
expected in the Rio Pescado.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

In hilly or mountainous terrain there are numerous low water
crossings which are potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.
